tasks.title: Initialize Expo Project with Dependencies
tasks.description: Set up the Expo managed workflow project with all required dependencies as specified in the PRD's tech stack, including React Native, expo-router, expo-secure-store, NativeWind, and all other packages.
tasks.details:
1. Run `npx create-expo-app stak-app --template blank-typescript` (or initialize in current directory)
2. Install Expo packages:
   ```bash
   npx expo install expo-secure-store expo-router expo-linking expo-status-bar react-native-screens react-native-safe-area-context react-native-svg
   ```
3. Install npm packages:
   ```bash
   npm install @tabler/icons-react-native axios zustand @tanstack/react-query react-hook-form @hookform/resolvers zod nativewind tailwindcss i18next react-i18next
   ```
4. Configure app.json with:
   - scheme: "stak"
   - expo-router plugin
   - proper bundleIdentifier/package names
5. Create tailwind.config.js with NativeWind v4 configuration
6. Configure babel.config.js for NativeWind
7. Update tsconfig.json with strict mode and path aliases
8. Create .env.local.example with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL and EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV
9. Create src/constants/api.ts with BASE_URL export reading from process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL
10. Ensure all version constraints match PRD §5.1
tasks.testStrategy: Verify: 1) `npx expo start --dev-client` launches without errors, 2) All dependencies listed in package.json match PRD versions, 3) TypeScript compiles with strict mode, 4) NativeWind classes render correctly on a test component, 5) Environment variables are accessible in the app.

export interface BaseResponse<T = unknown> {

tasks.title: Implement Secure Storage and Zustand Auth Store
tasks.description: Create the secure token storage layer using expo-secure-store with Zustand persist middleware adapter, and implement the complete auth store with hydration support.
tasks.details:
1. Implement src/lib/secure-store.ts:
   ```typescript
   import * as SecureStore from 'expo-secure-store'
   import { StateStorage } from 'zustand/middleware'
   export const TOKEN_KEY = 'stak_jwt'
   export const secureStore = {
     get: (key: string) => SecureStore.getItemAsync(key),
     set: (key: string, value: string) => SecureStore.setItemAsync(key, value),
     delete: (key: string) => SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(key),
   }
   export const zustandStorage: StateStorage = {
     getItem: (name) => SecureStore.getItem(name) ?? null,
     setItem: (name, value) => SecureStore.setItem(name, value),
     removeItem: (name) => SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(name),
   }
   ```
2. Implement src/stores/auth.store.ts with Zustand v5:
   - State: token, user (UserResource), isAuthenticated, isHydrated
   - Actions: setAuth, setToken, clearAuth, setHydrated
   - Use persist middleware with createJSONStorage(() => zustandStorage)
   - partialize to exclude isHydrated from persistence
   - onRehydrateStorage callback to call setHydrated()
3. Create src/hooks/useAuth.ts as thin wrapper exposing auth state/actions
4. Match implementation exactly to PRD §7.4 and §7.5
tasks.testStrategy: Verify: 1) Token persists across app restarts on both Android and iOS physical devices, 2) isHydrated transitions from false to true after SecureStore read completes, 3) clearAuth removes token from both Zustand state and SecureStore, 4) User data round-trips correctly through JSON serialization.

subtasks.title: Implement src/lib/secure-store.ts with SecureStore helpers and Zustand adapter
subtasks.description: Create the secure storage layer that wraps expo-secure-store with typed helper methods and implements the Zustand StateStorage adapter for persist middleware integration.
subtasks.details:
Create src/lib/secure-store.ts with the following implementation exactly matching PRD §7.4:

1. Import SecureStore from expo-secure-store and StateStorage from zustand/middleware
2. Export TOKEN_KEY constant as 'stak_jwt'
3. Export secureStore object with async methods:
   - get: (key: string) => SecureStore.getItemAsync(key)
   - set: (key: string, value: string) => SecureStore.setItemAsync(key, value)
   - delete: (key: string) => SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(key)
4. Export zustandStorage implementing StateStorage interface:
   - getItem: (name) => SecureStore.getItem(name) ?? null (synchronous for initial hydration)
   - setItem: (name, value) => SecureStore.setItem(name, value) (synchronous write)
   - removeItem: (name) => SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(name) (async delete is acceptable)

Note: zustandStorage uses the synchronous getItem/setItem methods from expo-secure-store for Zustand compatibility, while secureStore helpers use async methods for explicit API calls.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify: 1) TOKEN_KEY equals 'stak_jwt', 2) secureStore.set followed by secureStore.get returns the same value, 3) secureStore.delete removes the value, 4) zustandStorage.getItem returns null for non-existent keys (not undefined), 5) TypeScript compiles without errors with StateStorage type.

subtasks.title: Implement src/stores/auth.store.ts with Zustand v5 persist middleware
subtasks.description: Create the complete Zustand auth store with state (token, user, isAuthenticated, isHydrated), actions (setAuth, setToken, clearAuth, setHydrated), and persist middleware configuration using SecureStore.
subtasks.details:
Create src/stores/auth.store.ts following PRD §7.5 exactly:

1. Import create from 'zustand', persist/createJSONStorage from 'zustand/middleware', zustandStorage from '../lib/secure-store', and UserResource from '../types/user'
2. Define AuthState interface: token: string | null, user: UserResource | null, isAuthenticated: boolean, isHydrated: boolean
3. Define AuthActions interface: setAuth(token, user), setToken(token), clearAuth(), setHydrated()
4. Create useAuthStore using create<AuthState & AuthActions>()(
   persist(
     (set) => ({
       token: null, user: null, isAuthenticated: false, isHydrated: false,
       setAuth: (token, user) => set({ token, user, isAuthenticated: true }),
       setToken: (token) => set({ token }),
       clearAuth: () => set({ token: null, user: null, isAuthenticated: false }),
       setHydrated: () => set({ isHydrated: true }),
     }),
     {
       name: 'stak-auth',
       storage: createJSONStorage(() => zustandStorage),
       partialize: (state) => ({ token: state.token, user: state.user, isAuthenticated: state.isAuthenticated }),
       onRehydrateStorage: () => (state) => { state?.setHydrated() },
     }
   )
)
5. Export useAuthStore for use in components and API client
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify: 1) Initial state has isHydrated: false, 2) setAuth updates token, user, and isAuthenticated to true, 3) clearAuth resets token, user to null and isAuthenticated to false, 4) isHydrated is NOT persisted (partialize excludes it), 5) onRehydrateStorage callback sets isHydrated to true after SecureStore read.

subtasks.title: Implement src/hooks/useAuth.ts as thin wrapper for auth state and actions
subtasks.description: Create a custom React hook that provides a clean API for accessing auth state and actions from the Zustand store, abstracting the store implementation details from components.
subtasks.details:
Create src/hooks/useAuth.ts as a thin wrapper over useAuthStore:

1. Import useAuthStore from '../stores/auth.store'
2. Export useAuth hook that returns an object with:
   - State: token, user, isAuthenticated, isHydrated (directly from store)
   - Actions: setAuth, setToken, clearAuth (directly from store)
3. Use shallow comparison or selective subscriptions to prevent unnecessary re-renders:
   - Option A: Return useAuthStore() directly if all fields are needed
   - Option B: Use useAuthStore with selector for specific fields

Example implementation:
export function useAuth() {
  const { token, user, isAuthenticated, isHydrated, setAuth, setToken, clearAuth } = useAuthStore()
  return { token, user, isAuthenticated, isHydrated, setAuth, setToken, clearAuth }
}

This hook will be used by screens and components that need auth state without importing the store directly. It provides a stable API surface even if the underlying store implementation changes.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify: 1) useAuth returns all expected state properties (token, user, isAuthenticated, isHydrated), 2) useAuth returns all expected actions (setAuth, setToken, clearAuth), 3) Calling setAuth through useAuth updates state correctly, 4) Hook can be imported and used in React components without errors.

subtasks.title: Configure persist middleware rehydration and storage key naming
subtasks.description: Ensure the Zustand persist middleware correctly handles async rehydration from SecureStore, properly names storage keys, and handles JSON serialization/deserialization of the user object.
subtasks.details:
Verify and configure the persist middleware rehydration behavior:

1. Storage key: 'stak-auth' (configured in persist options name field)
2. JSON serialization: createJSONStorage handles JSON.stringify/parse automatically for the user object (UserResource with nested fields)
3. Rehydration flow:
   - App starts → isHydrated: false
   - Zustand persist reads from SecureStore via zustandStorage.getItem('stak-auth')
   - JSON is parsed, state is merged into store
   - onRehydrateStorage callback fires → setHydrated() called → isHydrated: true
4. Handle edge cases:
   - First launch (no stored data): state remains default, setHydrated still called
   - Corrupted JSON: createJSONStorage handles errors, defaults to initial state
   - SecureStore unavailable (web/simulator): graceful fallback needed
5. Verify partialize correctly excludes isHydrated from persistence to prevent stale hydration flags
6. Consider adding version field for future migrations if needed
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify: 1) Token persists across app restarts on Android (Samsung A34) and iOS (iPhone 15), 2) isHydrated transitions from false to true after SecureStore read completes, 3) User object with all UserResource fields round-trips correctly through JSON serialization, 4) First app launch with empty SecureStore still sets isHydrated to true.

subtasks.title: Add clearAuth integration with SecureStore deletion
subtasks.description: Ensure the clearAuth action not only clears Zustand state but also explicitly deletes the token from SecureStore to prevent stale tokens on next app launch.
subtasks.details:
Enhance clearAuth to ensure complete token removal:

1. Current clearAuth only clears Zustand state (token: null, user: null, isAuthenticated: false)
2. Zustand persist middleware will automatically sync this to storage via zustandStorage.setItem
3. However, for security, explicitly verify token deletion works:
   - The persist middleware should overwrite stored state with cleared values
   - TOKEN_KEY ('stak_jwt') from secure-store.ts should be cleared
4. Consider adding explicit SecureStore deletion in logout flow (in useAuthMutations, not here)
5. Test scenarios:
   - clearAuth → close app → reopen → should NOT be authenticated
   - clearAuth should work even if SecureStore write fails (network issues on some devices)
6. The clearAuth action in auth.store.ts remains simple state clearing; the persist middleware handles storage sync automatically
7. For explicit token deletion outside persist flow, use secureStore.delete(TOKEN_KEY) in the API logout function
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify: 1) clearAuth removes token from both Zustand state and SecureStore, 2) After clearAuth and app restart, user is redirected to login (not auto-logged-in), 3) SecureStore.getItemAsync(TOKEN_KEY) returns null after clearAuth, 4) clearAuth works on both Android and iOS physical devices.

tasks.title: Implement Axios Client with JWT Interceptors
tasks.description: Create the Axios HTTP client with JWT bearer token injection, automatic 401 refresh with queue pattern, and proper error handling for concurrent requests.
tasks.details:
1. Implement src/api/client.ts following PRD §7.6 exactly:
   ```typescript
   - Create axios instance with baseURL from constants, 15s timeout
   - Request interceptor: attach Bearer token from Zustand state (sync) or SecureStore fallback (async)
   - Response interceptor for 401 handling:
     - isRefreshing flag and failedQueue array
     - processQueue helper to resolve/reject queued requests
     - On 401: if isRefreshing, queue request; else set isRefreshing, call refresh endpoint
     - On refresh success: update token in Zustand + SecureStore, process queue, retry original
     - On refresh failure: clear auth, reject queue, let navigation guard handle redirect
   ```
2. Implement src/lib/error.ts:
   ```typescript
   export function extractProblem(error: unknown): ProblemDetail | null
   export function firstFieldError(problem: ProblemDetail, field: string): string | undefined
   ```
3. Handle edge case: _retry flag to prevent infinite refresh loops
4. Use standalone axios.post for refresh call (not apiClient) to avoid interceptor recursion
tasks.testStrategy: Verify: 1) Requests include Authorization header when token exists, 2) 401 triggers refresh and retries original request seamlessly, 3) Concurrent 401s queue properly and all resolve after single refresh, 4) Failed refresh clears auth state, 5) Token updates in both Zustand and SecureStore after refresh.

subtasks.title: Implement 401 response interceptor with refresh queue pattern
subtasks.description: Add response interceptor for 401 handling with refresh token queue pattern to handle concurrent requests, prevent infinite loops with _retry flag, and clear auth on refresh failure.
subtasks.details: Add to `src/api/client.ts`: module-level `isRefreshing` flag and `failedQueue` array; `processQueue(error, token)` helper that resolves/rejects all queued promises; response interceptor that on 401: (1) if _retry flag set, reject to prevent loop, (2) if isRefreshing, queue request and return promise, (3) else set isRefreshing=true, set original._retry=true, call standalone axios.post to BASE_URL + '/api/v1/auth/refresh' with current token (NOT apiClient to avoid recursion), on success update Zustand token via setToken(), update SecureStore, processQueue with new token, retry original; on failure processQueue with error, call clearAuth(), reject. Always set isRefreshing=false in finally block.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify single 401 triggers refresh and retries original request seamlessly. Verify concurrent 401s queue properly - only one refresh fires, all resolve after single refresh completes. Verify failed refresh clears auth state via clearAuth(). Verify _retry flag prevents infinite refresh loops. Verify token updates in both Zustand and SecureStore after successful refresh.

   ```typescript
   export async function resendVerification(): Promise<BaseResponse>
   ```

   ```typescript
     password: z.string().min(8, 'At least 8 characters'),

     path: ['passwordConfirmation'],
   })
   ```

subtasks.title: Integrate Login API Call and Success Handling
subtasks.description: Connect form submission to useAuthMutations().login mutation, handle successful authentication by storing token/user and navigating to protected app screens.

tasks.title: Implement i18n Localization System
tasks.description: Set up i18next with react-i18next, create locale files for en-US, nl, id, jv, and implement locale resolution from user/device/fallback with persistence.
tasks.details:
1. Create src/lib/i18n.ts:
   ```typescript
   import i18n from 'i18next'
   import { initReactI18next } from 'react-i18next'
   import * as Localization from 'expo-localization'
   import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage'
   // Import locale files
   // Configure with fallbackLng: 'en-US', interpolation: { escapeValue: false }
   ```
2. Create locale files in src/locales/:
   - en-US.json: All auth screen strings (Welcome back, Enter your details, etc.)
   - nl.json, id.json, jv.json: Translated versions
3. Implement locale resolution order (PRD §14.2):
   - user.locale from UserResource (authenticated)
   - AsyncStorage 'stak_locale' (guest preference)
   - expo-localization device locale
   - en-US fallback
4. Add locale key for AsyncStorage
5. Create useLocale hook for switching languages
6. Update auth store to sync locale with i18n on user change
tasks.testStrategy: Verify: 1) Default locale resolves correctly from device, 2) Authenticated user's locale from UserResource is applied, 3) Guest locale preference persists in AsyncStorage, 4) All auth screen strings use t() translations, 5) Language switch updates UI immediately.

subtasks.title: Auth Flows Manual Testing - Login, Register, Forgot Password
subtasks.description: Execute comprehensive manual tests for login, register, and forgot password flows on both physical devices per PRD §19 acceptance criteria.
subtasks.details:
1. Login flow testing (both devices):
   - Valid credentials: email + password → token stored, redirect to (app)/index
   - Invalid credentials: wrong password → 401 error shown, no redirect
   - Form validation: empty fields show 'required' errors, invalid email format shows error
   - Token persistence: close app, reopen → still authenticated, lands on (app)/index
   - Logout: tap logout → token cleared, redirect to login

2. Register flow testing (both devices):
   - Success: fill all fields correctly → success card shown, NOT auto-logged in
   - Validation errors: password < 8 chars, passwords don't match, invalid email
   - Server validation: existing email → 422 error with field-level message
   - Samsung A34 specific: confirm `autoComplete='new-password'` suppresses keyboard overlay on confirm-password

3. Forgot password flow testing (both devices):
   - Submit valid email → success card shown (enumeration-safe response regardless of email existence)
   - Resend cooldown: tap resend immediately → 429 rate limit error displayed
   - Validation: empty email → 'required' error, invalid format → 'invalid email' error

4. Document any platform-specific differences between Samsung A34 and iPhone 15
subtasks.testStrategy: Execute full test matrix: Login (valid/invalid/empty), Register (success/validation/duplicate email), Forgot Password (submit/resend/validation) on both devices. Document pass/fail for each test case with screenshots.

subtasks.title: Deep Link Testing - Reset Password and Email Verification
subtasks.description: Test deep link handling for reset password and email verification flows on both physical devices using the stak:// custom scheme.
subtasks.details:
1. Reset password deep link testing:
   - Generate test deep link: `stak://auth/reset-password?token=xxx&email=test@example.com`
   - Samsung A34: open link via adb `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d 'stak://auth/reset-password?token=xxx&email=test@example.com'`
   - iPhone 15: open link via Safari or npx uri-scheme open

   - Valid token: submit new password → success, can login with new password
   - Expired/invalid token: submit → 400/422 error displayed to user

   - App in background → resume and navigate to correct screen

subtasks.title: Cross-Cutting Concerns Testing - Token Refresh, Cold Start, UI Interactions
subtasks.description: Validate cross-cutting concerns including silent token refresh, cold start hydration, keyboard behavior, and eye toggle touch targets on both devices.
subtasks.details:
1. Token refresh testing:
   - Login successfully, note token expiry time
   - Wait for token to expire OR manually trigger 401 (e.g., invalidate token on server)
   - Perform authenticated action → should silently refresh and succeed
   - Verify: no user-visible interruption, new token stored in SecureStore
   - Multiple concurrent 401s: trigger several simultaneous requests → only ONE refresh call, all requests succeed after
   - Refresh failure: force refresh endpoint to fail → user logged out, redirected to login

2. Cold start / hydration testing:
   - Kill app completely (not just background)
   - Reopen app with valid token in SecureStore
   - Verify: splash screen shown until `isHydrated: true`
   - After hydration: authenticated user lands on (app)/index, unauthenticated lands on login
   - No flash of wrong screen (no login → home flash or vice versa)

3. Keyboard behavior testing:
   - Open login screen, tap email field → keyboard appears
   - All form fields should remain visible above keyboard (KeyboardAwareView)
   - Samsung A34: `behavior='height'` should work correctly
   - iPhone 15: `behavior='padding'` should work correctly
   - Test on register form (more fields) to ensure scrolling works if needed

4. Eye toggle / touch target testing:
   - Password fields have eye toggle icon (20×20dp)
   - Tap eye toggle → password visibility toggles
   - Touch target must be 44×44dp minimum (hitSlop configured)
   - Test on both devices: toggle should respond to taps reliably
subtasks.testStrategy: Token: force 401, verify silent refresh. Cold start: kill app, reopen, verify correct routing. Keyboard: fill forms, verify visibility. Eye toggle: tap repeatedly, verify consistent response. Document any platform-specific issues.
